name: 143-tile-classification.svg
title: A tile is a set of sample centres
desc: A triangle crosses a four by four tile grid. Tiles wholly inside are teal, tiles outside remain pale, and inconclusive tiles are amber; the exact sample mask still determines the result.
marker: ## A small triangle can have a large attribute gradient

name: 144-shared-diagonal-mask.svg
title: Two masks, one complete square
desc: An eight by eight miniature of the guided rectangle fixture displays one triangle owning every diagonal sample, with the other owning only the strict opposite half.

name: 145-depth-pyramid.svg
title: The depth hierarchy keeps a conservative bound
desc: Four leaf maxima 0.35, 0.55, 0.75, and 1.00 feed a root maximum of 1.00. A candidate depth of 0.58 can reject only the first two leaves under strict forward depth.
marker: ## Why depth precision changes across the picture

name: 146-depth-interval-scaling.svg
title: Depth resolution grows quadratically
desc: The plotted relative axial interval follows d squared for fixed uniformly spaced depth values. Distances of 1, 10 and 100 units give interval ratios of 1, 100 and 10000.

name: 147-reconstruction-aliasing.svg
title: Averaging restores the correct light
desc: An alternating linear signal gives phase-dependent point samples of zero or one, while the exact two-texel average is one half for each output sample.
marker: ## Choose a texture level from a projected footprint

name: 148-anisotropic-footprint.svg
title: One screen pixel, unequal texel stretches
desc: The eight by one ellipse spans eight texels horizontally and one vertically, while an isotropic footprint of equal major radius also averages across the short axis.

name: 149-sample-pipeline.svg
title: One sample, five independently testable stages
desc: The single triangle witness is followed from optical coordinates through projected barycentrics, reciprocal-w, depth, and the final color encoding decision.
marker: ## A small scene is a better specification than a large screenshot

name: 150-perspective-weight-witness.svg
title: Screen weights are not surface weights
desc: Paired horizontal bars contrast the screen barycentric weights with perspective-correct weights for the numerical triangle witness. The latter reconstruct the original viewing ray.

name: 151-focus-sweep.svg
title: Near and far focus blur are asymmetric
desc: At the fixed sensor position for a 1000 mm object, a 50 mm thin lens and 12.5 mm aperture produce geometric blur diameters that vanish at focus and increase asymmetrically with object distance.
marker: ## A camera records a spread, not a perfect point

name: 152-aperture-area-sampling.svg
title: Uniform radius is not uniform area
desc: Equal-width radial bands have areas proportional to 1, 3, 5 and 7. Equal probabilities per band overrepresent the central region; uniform-area sampling gives probabilities proportional to band area.

name: 153-angular-projection-comparison.svg
title: Different angular maps agree near the axis
desc: Five normalized angular projection laws are plotted from zero to sixty degrees. Their common slope at zero hides important differences at the edge of the field.
marker: ## Inverse angular projection returns a ray, not a point

name: 154-inverse-uncertainty.svg
title: Undistortion stretches uncertainty unequally
desc: An isotropic half-pixel input uncertainty becomes an ellipse whose radial standard deviation is approximately 0.588 pixels and tangential standard deviation 0.526 pixels in the given local model.

name: 155-photon-transfer-fit.svg
title: The slope measures conversion gain
desc: The analytic unsaturated temporal variance line has slope 0.5 digital units per electron and intercept 4 digital units squared. The four plotted points are model values, not camera measurements.
marker: ## A saturated value carries an inequality

name: 156-sensor-clipping-bound.svg
title: A saturated code gives an inequality
desc: For gain 0.5 and black offset 64, a maximum code of 255 is reached at 382 electrons. Larger signals map to the same output in this noiseless model.

name: 157-color-calibration-rank.svg
title: Independent color directions constrain a matrix
desc: Three independent artificial sensor responses constrain a three-channel transform. Neutral observations remain on one line and cannot identify the other two directions.
marker: ## White adaptation is a change of viewing condition, not a universal correction

name: 158-color-clipping-loss.svg
title: Clipping destroys invertibility
desc: With gain two, input red channels 0.6 and 0.8 both map to output one after clipping. The unclipped linear transform is invertible, but its clipped form is not.

name: 159-calibration-sensitivity.svg
title: Calibration spread separates focal scale
desc: Two centered three-point designs have normalized coordinate spread differing by ten. Their focal parameter variance differs by a factor of one hundred for equal pixel noise.
marker: ## Why damping is not the same as observing more data

name: 160-normal-matrix-eigenvalues.svg
title: Correlation creates a weak parameter direction
desc: The strong eigenvalue is 1 plus correlation, and the weak eigenvalue is 1 minus correlation. At correlation 0.99 the weak eigenvalue falls to 0.01.

name: 161-rectification-rows.svg
title: Rectification aligns epipolar rows
desc: Two image planes show corresponding points on a common horizontal row after rectification. Their horizontal separation is disparity, not a proof that the correspondence is correct.
marker: ## Disparity is a measurement with its own uncertainty

name: 162-disparity-nonlinearity.svg
title: Small disparities create asymmetric depth intervals
desc: Depth equals 80 divided by disparity for the stated focal scale and baseline. Near two pixels, a plus or minus half-pixel disparity interval maps to 32 through 53.33 metres.

name: 163-scale-normalized-blob.svg
title: A Gaussian blob has a characteristic scale
desc: The scale-normalized Laplacian magnitude for ideal blobs of widths two and four peaks at their respective widths, with equal peak response one half.
marker: ## A descriptor is a choice about what to forget

name: 164-matching-denominators.svg
title: The matching stages use different denominators
desc: The illustrative twenty-feature fixture retains sixteen repeated detections, twelve correct retrievals, and eleven verified true matches. Two false matches survive separately.

name: 165-inverse-depth-response.svg
title: Inverse depth linearizes rectified disparity
desc: For focal scale 800 pixels and baseline 0.1 metres, disparity is linear in inverse axial depth. A zero inverse depth is a limiting direction rather than a finite metric point.

name: 166-schur-blocks.svg
title: Eliminate landmark variables, not their evidence
desc: The toy normal matrix has a camera block of two, two landmark diagonal blocks of two, and camera-landmark coupling one. Eliminating the landmarks leaves a scalar camera coefficient of one.

name: 167-sparse-block-boundaries.svg
title: An edge can cross a sparse-block boundary
desc: Two allocated voxel blocks share a global edge crossing while a third unallocated block remains unknown. Local cell indices and global edge identity must not be confused.
marker: ## Extracting a mesh is a second inference

name: 168-weighted-crossing-support.svg
title: The zero must be supported by observations
desc: The guided axial fixture gives field values one, one half and minus one half at depths 0.9, 1.0 and 1.1 metres. The 1.2 metre sample has zero weight and no defined observation.

name: 169-dependency-invalidation.svg
title: An encoding edit need not invalidate geometry
desc: A chain from geometry and camera to projection, coverage, linear color and encoding shows the dependencies. A transfer-only change invalidates only the final encoded output.

name: 170-stale-snapshot-result.svg
title: An old result must retain its own identity
desc: Snapshot A starts first, snapshot B starts later and finishes first. The late A result cannot overwrite B as if it were the current camera state.

name: 171-speedup-aggregation.svg
title: Two valid summaries answer different questions
desc: For the two hypothetical workloads, scene-level speedups are two and 0.909. The geometric mean is about 1.348 while the ratio of total elapsed times is about 0.914.
marker: ## A numerical claim needs an error budget

name: 172-ablation-evidence.svg
title: An ablation must preserve the question
desc: A common input set feeds both baseline and modified pipelines. Their surviving support and numerical errors are compared before interpreting measured cost.
